events.text_en: When Thiên Xu breaks Thiết Tỏa Quan, the smith Vưu Liên Hoàn is standing on his chain, and goes down with it to the river bed.
A twelve-year-old girl walks from the drowned Abbey of Still Water to Tùng Đào with its altar lamp, which she has dug out of the river mud.
A fisher's boy of Hàn Tân swims the river mouth to Thúy Vi. The governor Giáp Tùng Chi takes the next boy on the street into the pines.
When the Cold Ford is given up, its governor Giáp Tùng Chi will not leave his quay and dies on it. His disciple carries the governor's seal out of the town.
An old ward-singer of Tùng Đào's Array Hall dies in closed-door seclusion, and three ward-songs no one else had heard go with him.
Nhiếp Thừa Phong of Tùng Đào cuts every rope bridge on the Ngư Ca border and is killed on the last; Lạc Hà sends his flying blade back without him.
An outer disciple of Tùng Đào, a woodcutter's son, says the pines above Tùng Hạ Thị are chanting something longer than the primer.
A rope-hand of Tùng Đào's Coiled Root Hall, who held the windlass line on the night of the last Ngư Ca bridge, crosses to the Lạc Hà bank on an unsigned word in spring and does not come back.
